eligibility_reason: The paper reports original survey-based estimates of prior recognition of disinformation narratives and self-reported sharing among adults in the Czech Republic. Estimates are based on data collected in June 2023.

estimates.measure: share reporting no prior recognition of any of seven disinformation narratives
estimates.misinfo_definition: False information communicated as true and intentionally communicated as true to influence people’s beliefs or behavior; the study used seven real, actively circulating misinformation or disinformation narratives.
estimates.source_quote: Approximately one third of participants (34.2 %) reported not recognizing any of the seven disinformation narratives presented.

estimates.measure: share recognizing five or more of seven disinformation narratives
estimates.misinfo_definition: False information communicated as true and intentionally communicated as true to influence people’s beliefs or behavior; the study used seven real, actively circulating misinformation or disinformation narratives.
estimates.source_quote: In contrast, 6.5 % recognized five or more.

estimates.measure: share reporting no prior exposure to any of seven disinformation narratives
estimates.misinfo_definition: False information communicated as true and intentionally communicated as true to influence people’s beliefs or behavior; the study used seven real, actively circulating misinformation or disinformation narratives.
estimates.source_quote: In contrast, 53 % of the youngest participants (aged 16–24) reported no prior exposure to any of the seven disinformation narratives.

estimates.measure: upper bound on the share seeing narratives F and C
estimates.misinfo_definition: False information communicated as true and intentionally communicated as true to influence people’s beliefs or behavior; the study used seven real, actively circulating misinformation or disinformation narratives.
estimates.source_quote: While some disinformation narratives (e.g., G and A) were encountered by more than one-third of participants, others (e.g., F and C) were seen by fewer than 12 %.
estimates.notes: Printed as a bound; applies to narratives F and C.

estimates.measure: share reporting sharing at least one disinformation narrative
estimates.misinfo_definition: False information communicated as true and intentionally communicated as true to influence people’s beliefs or behavior; the study used seven real, actively circulating misinformation or disinformation narratives.
estimates.source_quote: Across the entire sample, only 10 % of participants (N = 310) reported sharing at least one disinformation narrative.

estimates.denominator: participants who had encountered at least one disinformation item
estimates.measure: share reporting no sharing of encountered disinformation narratives
estimates.misinfo_definition: False information communicated as true and intentionally communicated as true to influence people’s beliefs or behavior; the study used seven real, actively circulating misinformation or disinformation narratives.
estimates.source_quote: Among those who had encountered at least one disinformation item (N = 2131), the majority (86 %) did not share any, while 3.2 % (N = 68) reported sharing all the disinformation narratives they had encountered.

estimates.denominator: participants who had encountered at least one disinformation item
estimates.measure: share reporting sharing all encountered disinformation narratives
estimates.misinfo_definition: False information communicated as true and intentionally communicated as true to influence people’s beliefs or behavior; the study used seven real, actively circulating misinformation or disinformation narratives.
estimates.source_quote: Among those who had encountered at least one disinformation item (N = 2131), the majority (86 %) did not share any, while 3.2 % (N = 68) reported sharing all the disinformation narratives they had encountered.

estimates.measure: share of recognized disinformation narratives reported as shared
estimates.misinfo_definition: False information communicated as true and intentionally communicated as true to influence people’s beliefs or behavior; the study used seven real, actively circulating misinformation or disinformation narratives.
estimates.source_quote: On average, participants shared 0.18 disinformation items (SD = 0.70), corresponding to 8.2 % of the recognized disinformation narratives (SD = 22.4 %).

estimates.measure: share reporting sharing at least one disinformation narrative
estimates.misinfo_definition: False information communicated as true and intentionally communicated as true to influence people’s beliefs or behavior; the study used seven real, actively circulating misinformation or disinformation narratives.
estimates.source_quote: Similar proportions of men (9.0 %) and women (10.1 %) reported sharing at least one disinformation narrative (χ2 (1) = 0.975, p = .324, OR = 1.13, 95 % CI: 0.89–1.42; see Supplementary Table S6).

estimates.measure: share reporting sharing at least one disinformation narrative
estimates.misinfo_definition: False information communicated as true and intentionally communicated as true to influence people’s beliefs or behavior; the study used seven real, actively circulating misinformation or disinformation narratives.
estimates.source_quote: Similar proportions of men (9.0 %) and women (10.1 %) reported sharing at least one disinformation narrative (χ2 (1) = 0.975, p = .324, OR = 1.13, 95 % CI: 0.89–1.42; see Supplementary Table S6).

estimates.measure: share of encountered disinformation reported as shared
estimates.misinfo_definition: False information communicated as true and intentionally communicated as true to influence people’s beliefs or behavior; the study used seven real, actively circulating misinformation or disinformation narratives.
estimates.source_quote: Similarly, the proportion of shared disinformation was highest among the least educated group (13.4 %) and lowest among those with university education (3.7 %).

estimates.misinfo_definition: False information communicated as true and intentionally communicated as true to influence people’s beliefs or behavior; the study used seven real, actively circulating misinformation or disinformation narratives.
estimates.source_quote: Similarly, the proportion of shared disinformation was highest among the least educated group (13.4 %) and lowest among those with university education (3.7 %).
